managers.s: Concentrated value · Private deals · Long holding periods David worked under Seth Klarman at Baupost before starting Abrams Capital in 1999. Loar, the aerospace parts maker he backed before its 2024 IPO, is 41% of the 13F.

Quality compounders · IRR hurdle · Concentrated core Chris models 120 to 150 companies in his Grove of Titans and buys when one reaches a 15% ten-year IRR. His fund holds about eight; the 13F lists every account the firm manages, 81 positions.

Value · Diversified · Gold and hard assets Arnold's 13F holds about 120 stocks, and gold has a steady place in it: the Sprott Physical Gold Trust is the biggest holding and Seabridge Gold has been there since 2013. Berkshire is in every 13F since 2013.

Contrarian · Very concentrated · Real estate and financials St. Joe, the Florida land company, is 76% of Bruce's 13F. It's in every one since 2013, and it went from 7% of the portfolio to as much as 99%.
Quality at a discount · Conservative appraisals · Concentrated One letter a year, often 100+ pages, with the Berkshire Hathaway valuation serious Berkshire watchers wait for. Block an afternoon.

Private-equity mindset · Mid caps · Trims and adds around value Turtle Creek has compounded since 1998 doing something closer to private equity than classic value. Andrew explains why trimming and adding around intrinsic value beats plain buy-and-hold.
Quality compounders · Europe and the US · Long term Nicolai Tangen started AKO in 2005 and left in 2020 to run Norway's oil fund. Ferrari and Visa are in every 13F since the first, in 2016.

Deep value · Distressed debt · Holds cash when it's expensive Francis holds cash when he can't find bargains and buys distressed debt only when the recovery is there, and his letters say plainly what went wrong. Berkshire is in every 13F since 2013 and is 30% of it now.

Value · Diversified · Family office Lee ran Goldman Sachs Asset Management before he started Omega in 1991, and since 2019 the firm manages only his family's money. Vertiv, held since 2020, is 16% of the 13F.

Quality at fair prices · Financials · Long holding periods Chris is the third generation of Davises to run the firm, and he says all real investing is value investing; the rest is speculation. Berkshire, American Express, Wells Fargo, Markel and Alphabet are in every 13F since 2013.

Wide moats · Long runways · Concentrated Pat wrote the book on moats at Morningstar. His fund holds 10 to 15 businesses with a moat, a long runway and managers who allocate capital well; Meta is in every 13F since his first, in 2016.

Value · Long-short · Macro Greenlight runs a long-short book with a macro sleeve, and the 13F shows only the longs. Green Brick Partners, the homebuilder David helped launch in 2014, is in every one since 2013 and is the biggest position at 19%.

Quality compounders · Buy and hold · Diversified Tom has run Markel's stock portfolio since 1990 and became CEO in 2023. He wants profitable businesses, honest and able managers, room to reinvest and a fair price; 14 stocks, Berkshire, Visa and Home Depot among them, are in every 13F since 2013.

Quality businesses · Concentrated · Long holding periods Glenn's firm was called Chieftain Capital before it became Brave Warrior. Primerica is in every one of his 13Fs since 2013, longer than any other stock he owns.

Quantitative value · Very diversified · Rules-based Joel wrote The Little Book That Beats the Market and teaches at Columbia. Gotham now runs a diversified, rules-based book of about 1,800 stocks; this page shows the 50 biggest.

Deep value · Obscure and out of favor · Long holding periods Irving Kahn was Ben Graham's teaching assistant at Columbia and started the firm with his sons in 1978; he died in 2015, at 109. The firm still looks for the obscure and the out of favor, and Citigroup, Merck, Pfizer, BP and Exxon Mobil are in every 13F since 2013.

Small caps · Hidden assets · Activism Connor started Alta Fox in 2018 to find small caps with a hidden asset inside. He wants about a 20% return a year without help from the multiple and sells when the multiple does the work; of today's holdings, only Daktronics goes back before 2025.

managers.f: Warren Buffett, Greg Abel and Ted Weschler
managers.s: Quality businesses · Fair prices · Permanent capital Greg Abel has been CEO since January 2026, but Warren still picks stocks; he says he started the Alphabet stake. American Express, Coca-Cola and Moody's are in every 13F since 2013.

Business, people, price · Concentrated · Long holding periods Mason founded Southeastern in 1975 and still chairs it; Ross Glotzbach runs it day to day. FedEx, CNX Resources and Graham Holdings are in every 13F since 2013.

Quality monopolies · Concentrated · Activist when needed Chris throws out most of the market before he starts: banks, airlines, utilities, commodities. He owns a handful of what's left for years; Moody's is in every 13F TCI has filed, back to 2015.
Activist · Controlled companies · Concentrated Most of Carl's 13F is his own companies: Icahn Enterprises and CVR Energy are 86% of it and in every filing since 2013. The rest is his activist stakes.

Contrarian value · Two- to three-year horizon · Concentrated Ed looks for change nobody expects and for a gap between how a company is seen and what it is. He has owned homebuilders on and off since 1987; Lennar, Toll Brothers, PulteGroup and D.R. Horton are more than a third of the 13F.

Quality compounders · Very concentrated · Buffett and Munger school Dev invests the Buffett and Munger way: about 10 businesses that work like toll booths, held for years. S&P Global, Moody's, Mastercard and Visa are in every 13F since his first, in 2016, and the two rating agencies are 38% of it.

Deep value · Distressed and special situations · Holds cash Seth wrote Margin of Safety in 1991 and still runs Baupost, which does much of its work in distressed debt, private deals and real estate that a 13F doesn't show. Amazon, bought in late 2025, is now the biggest position.

Quality at a discount · Buys in a crisis · Concentrated Bryan buys great businesses (a natural monopoly, a rational duopoly or the low-cost operator) when a crisis of confidence cuts the price. Interactive Brokers is in every 13F since his first, in 2017.

Quality at fair prices · Very concentrated · Buy and hold Norbert started Punch Card in 2004 and named it after Buffett's punch card: a few big decisions in a lifetime. His 13F has never held more than seven stocks, and Berkshire is usually the biggest.

Deep research · Very concentrated · US and Asia Li Lu says you'll probably have five or ten real insights in your life, and he bets big on the few he has. Most quarters his 13F holds nine stocks or fewer.

Quality compounders · Great managers who reinvest · Long holding periods Chuck Akre's three-legged stool (a great business, great managers, great reinvestment) still runs the firm under John Neff. Mastercard and Moody's are in every 13F since mid-2013, and Mastercard is still the biggest position.

Deep value · Safe and cheap · Real estate and cyclicals Marty Whitman built Third Avenue on what he called safe and cheap: a very strong balance sheet, bought below net asset value. He died in 2018. Brookfield and First Industrial Realty are in every 13F since 2013.

Quality at a discount · Shareholder-friendly businesses · Holds cash Don Yacktman founded the firm in 1992; his son Stephen and Jason Subotky run it now. They buy shareholder-friendly businesses at a discount, and Berkshire, Coca-Cola, PepsiCo and Procter & Gamble are in every 13F since 2013.

Distressed debt · Credit · Special situations Howard co-founded Oaktree in 1995 to buy the debt other investors wouldn't touch, and his memos are worth reading on their own. Most of Oaktree's money is in credit, so the 13F shows only a slice: listed stocks, many received in restructurings, and convertible bonds.

Quality compounders · Very concentrated · Low turnover AltaRock owns a handful of businesses and rarely sells. TransDigm, Mastercard, Visa and Moody's are in every 13F since the first, in 2014, and Microsoft and Amazon are now 60% of it.

Deep value · Small and micro caps · Hidden assets Mike buys overlooked small caps near their floor value, often with land or buildings the market has forgotten, and keeps about 15 of them. Alico, Amrep, Canterbury Park and Saga Communications are in every 13F since his first, in late 2023.

Small caps · Special situations · Concentrated Scott writes like he's talking to a friend and he's honest about how much of any record is luck. He also visits companies most investors only read about.

Deep value · Cloning · Very concentrated Mohnish's 13F shows only the US-listed slice of his funds. Right now that's four stocks, and two coal miners, Warrior Met Coal and Alpha Metallurgical, are more than half of it.

Deep value · Cyclicals and hard assets · Small and mid caps Bob's 13F leans on housing, building products and offshore energy. Builders FirstSource, Cavco, LSB Industries and Jefferies are in every one since 2013, and Tidewater is now 31% of it.

Quality growth · Long term · About 25 stocks François's annual letter tracks the owner earnings of every holding, and every year he reminds partners that trailing the market some years is the price of doing this well.
Quality growth · Concentrated, about 20 stocks Dave pairs holding-by-holding notes with blunt commentary on the Fed and valuations, and follows the same companies for years.

Global consumer brands · Family-controlled companies · Long holding periods Tom's 13F changes slowly. Berkshire, Philip Morris, Mastercard, Richemont, Heineken and Nestlé are in every one since 2013, the oldest on file.
Quality compounders · Buy and hold · Low turnover Terry's annual letter is short, funny and blunt, and he defends the strategy hardest in the years it isn't working.

Quality at a discount · Contrarian · Very concentrated Cliff has owned Carvana since early 2018, and it's now 79% of his 13F. The filing has never listed more than seven positions; Hilton Grand Vacations is the other big one.

Quality at fair prices · Concentrated · Low turnover Guy and Mohnish Pabrai bought a lunch with Buffett in 2008, and Guy's portfolio still shows it. Berkshire, American Express, Bank of America and Mastercard are in every 13F from his first, in 2014, to mid-2022, when Aquamarine stopped filing.

Index-like · Global · Sovereign wealth fund Nicolai founded AKO Capital and has run Norway's oil fund since 2020. The fund owns about 1.5% of every listed company in the world, so its 13F looks a lot like the US market. Some quarters it files the holdings a year late, under confidential treatment; they show up here when they come out.

Quality compounders · Very concentrated · Long holding periods Josh runs Greenlea Lane alone, with no office, and buys every stock as if he'll own it forever. He writes about what a spreadsheet misses: culture, quality, why people want a product.

Quality compounders · Ecosystem moats · Concentrated Chris says the medium is the moat: the edge is the ecosystem a company builds around its product. He has known Brad Jacobs since 1997, and QXO is his second-biggest position.
Quality compounders · Owner-operators · Concentrated Rob puts management character at the center of every decision and is candid about drawdowns, including a near-50% one.
Deep value · Worldwide, often emerging markets · Out-of-favor industries Amit spent decades at Third Avenue and still hunts where the discounts are widest, often in markets most US funds won't touch.

Contrarian value · Insurance float · Macro hedges Prem has run Fairfax since 1985 and invests its insurance float the way Berkshire does. The 13F shows only its US-listed stakes; two gold miners, Equinox Gold and Eldorado Gold, are now 44% of it.

Quality at fair prices · Concentrated · Long holding periods Wally started Weitz in Omaha in 1983 and moved over the years from cheap stocks toward quality businesses. Berkshire, Alphabet, Aon and Texas Instruments are in every 13F since 2013.
